fringe_towns.distance_note: ~22 miles NW of downtown Augusta, in Columbia County. Note: aggregator sites (Kayak, Hotels.com, HotelPlanner) list 'Harlem, GA' hotel results that are actually Augusta/Grovetown properties (Howard Johnson Augusta, Hampton Inn & Suites Augusta West, avid hotel Augusta W - Grovetown, Comfort Inn & Suites Augusta West Near Fort Eisenhower) geo-clustered by zip proximity, not physically located in Harlem town limits.
fringe_towns.notes: The one confirmed in-town lodging property (Red Oak Manor B&B) markets under its own name, not 'Augusta'. Harlem is also known as the birthplace of Oliver Hardy (Laurel & Hardy Museum).

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~18 miles NW of downtown Augusta, in Columbia County (per Visit Columbia County GA). Legal county seat of Columbia County but unincorporated, population 658 (2020 census); de facto commercial center of the county is Evans, not Appling.
fringe_towns.notes: No hotels/motels physically located in Appling. Aggregator pages titled 'Hotels in Appling, GA' (Choice Hotels, Reservations.com, HotelPlanner) actually surface properties in Augusta, Grovetown, and Thomson by zip-code/regional proximity — confirmed by the official Visit Columbia County GA page for Appling, which lists no lodging and only links out to a county-wide 'Book Now' accommodations search. Appling has zero hotel inventory of its own.

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~12 miles SW of downtown Augusta; Hephzibah is an incorporated city within Richmond County, part of the Augusta-Richmond County consolidated government area, near I-20 Exit 194.
fringe_towns.notes: This property's own brand name explicitly blends both 'Hephzibah' and 'Augusta' (Rodeway Inn & Suites Hephzibah Augusta), confirming it markets to Augusta search traffic while sitting in Hephzibah. Other names surfaced in initial aggregator summaries (an 'Econo Lodge' and a 'Super 8' 'in Hephzibah') could NOT be confirmed at a real Hephzibah street address on follow-up search — treat those as unverified/likely aggregator noise; only the Rodeway Inn address was independently confirmed via LoopNet/HotelPlanner listings on Deans Bridge Rd.

fringe_towns.distance_note: Not a separate town — confirmed to be a neighborhood/CDP within Augusta-Richmond County, roughly 6-8 miles west of downtown Augusta off Wheeler Rd / Belair Rd near I-20 Exit 194.
fringe_towns.notes: Belair is a residential suburban neighborhood/census-designated place inside the Augusta-Richmond County consolidated government, not an independent municipality. No distinct 'Belair' hotel market exists; any lodging in the area is simply part of the Augusta hotel inventory. Should NOT be treated as a separate fringe town for census purposes.

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~35 miles W of downtown Augusta, in McDuffie County, just off I-20.
fringe_towns.notes: Thomson has a real, multi-brand hotel base and every property markets under 'Thomson' in its own name, not 'Augusta'. Marketing copy references Augusta only as a nearby attraction (e.g., 'near Augusta National'), not as part of the hotel's identity.

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~45 miles W of downtown Augusta, in Jefferson County.
fringe_towns.notes: Only one confirmed in-town property (Western Motel), independently branded under the town/its own name, not 'Augusta'.

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~30 miles SE of downtown Augusta, in Burke County ('Bird Dog Capital of the World').
fringe_towns.notes: All confirmed Waynesboro properties brand under 'Waynesboro'. Marketing copy notes proximity to Augusta National ('30 miles from Augusta National Golf Club') as a selling point, but the hotel names/identities are Waynesboro-based, not Augusta-based.

fringe_towns.distance_note: ~45 miles N of downtown Augusta, in Lincoln County (near Clarks Hill/Strom Thurmond Lake).
fringe_towns.notes: All confirmed Lincolnton properties use town/lake-oriented or independent names, not 'Augusta'.

masters_event_housing.summary: Confirmed via search: the large majority of 'Masters week housing' inventory in the Augusta market is private home/estate rentals booked through dedicated event-housing marketplaces and agencies, NOT hotel rooms. Multiple sources describe a distinct, high-dollar short-term-rental market that operates only around the Masters (early April): one report cites over 16,400 rental nights booked on platforms like Airbnb/Vrbo in a single Masters week, worth roughly $8.5 million, with average nightly rates around $514 (vs. ~$200 normally) and some whole-house weekly rentals reaching $30,000+. This inventory (private homes, host homes, estates, condos) is fundamentally different from a hotel/motel census and must be EXCLUDED from any hotel directory build — including it would conflate residential short-term-rental listings with actual lodging-industry hotel properties.
example_marketplaces_for_exclusion_refer: Masters Housing Bureau (mastershousing.com) - the longstanding, Augusta National/Augusta Metro Chamber-linked official home-rental partner, ~50 years operating
Rent Like A Champion (rentlikeachampion.com) - private home rental and hospitality packages for Augusta/Masters
Champion Home Rentals (championhomerentals.com) - host homes, estates, and condos for Masters week
Tournament Housing (tournamenthousing.net) - short-term home rental connector for Masters week
Sports Traveler (sportstraveler.net) - luxury private home rental listings for the Masters
masters_event_housing.note: These are event-driven private-home rental marketplaces, not hotel brands or properties, and should never be added as 'hotels' to the census. Ordinary hotels near Augusta National do also raise Masters-week rates, but that is a pricing phenomenon, not a change in inventory type.

fort_gordon_rename.summary: Fort Gordon was officially redesignated Fort Eisenhower on October 27, 2023, in a renaming ceremony held on Barton Field at the installation. It was the last of nine U.S. Army posts to be renamed away from a Confederate namesake (Gordon was named for Confederate general John Brown Gordon) under the congressionally mandated renaming process. Despite the 2023 official rename, many nearby businesses/hotels still use 'Fort Gordon' in their names, URLs, and online listings today (as of this research, September 2026) — e.g., search results for hotels near the base still surface listings like 'Super 8 by Wyndham Augusta/Ft Gordon Area,' 'Holiday Inn Express & Suites Augusta West - Ft Gordon Area,' and 'Days Inn by Wyndham Augusta/Fort Gordon' alongside newer 'Near Fort Eisenhower' branding (e.g., 'Comfort Inn & Suites Augusta West Near Fort Eisenhower'). This means both 'Fort Gordon' and 'Fort Eisenhower' name variants coexist in current hotel marketing and should both be treated as valid geography/keyword references for the Augusta hotel census.
